Types of seagoing ship.Tanker: The largest supertankers can carry about two million barrels of oil, and they take miles to stop.
Types of seagoing ship.Container ship: Standardized steel boxes from Malcolm McLean's 1956 idea cut shipping costs enormously, and today's biggest ships carry over 20,000 boxes.
Types of seagoing ship.Cruise ship: Modern cruise ships are floating resorts that can hold over 6,000 passengers and thousands of crew.
Types of seagoing ship.Ferry: Ferries carry people and vehicles across short water routes, and Staten Island's ferry in New York is free to ride.
Types of seagoing ship.Icebreaker: Icebreakers use a strong, reinforced hull and heavy weight to ride up on ice and crack it from above; some are nuclear powered.
Types of seagoing ship.Trawler: A trawler drags a large net behind it to catch fish, and the largest factory trawlers can process catch onboard.
Types of seagoing ship.Tugboat: Tugs are small but extremely powerful, and can guide or tow ships hundreds of times their size.
Types of seagoing ship.Hospital ship: Under the Geneva Conventions, hospital ships are painted white with red crosses and must not be attacked.
Types of seagoing ship.Battleship: Battleships were the dominant naval weapon until aircraft carriers surpassed them in World War II.
Types of seagoing ship.Ocean liner: Liners were built for fast, scheduled crossings, as against cruise ships made for leisure; the Titanic was one such liner.
Types of seagoing ship.Dredger: Dredgers scoop sand and silt from waterways to keep channels deep, and they also build artificial islands.
Types of seagoing ship.Airliner: A trap: an airliner flies, so it is no ship at sea. The Boeing 747 and Airbus A380 are the most famous.
Types of seagoing ship.Jumbo jet: The 'jumbo jet' nickname fits the Boeing 747, which entered service in 1970 and is an aircraft, not a ship.
Types of seagoing ship.Bomber: A bomber is a military aircraft; it flies, not sails, and the B-52 has been in service since the 1950s.
Types of seagoing ship.Glider: A glider has no engine, and uses rising air to stay aloft, which is why it can fly but can't sail.
Types of seagoing ship.Blimp: A blimp is a non-rigid airship that gets lift from gas; it floats in the air, not at sea.
Types of seagoing ship.Biplane: A biplane has two stacked wings, and was the standard aircraft design in the Wright brothers era and World War I.
Types of seagoing ship.Cargo plane: Cargo planes carry freight through the air, which is faster than a ship but far more expensive.
Types of seagoing ship.Spitfire: A trap: the Spitfire was a famous British fighter plane of World War II, so it flies rather than sails.
Types of seagoing ship.Seaplane: A seaplane lands and takes off on water, which tempts players, but it is still an aircraft, not a ship.
Types of seagoing ship.Airship: An airship floats using lifting gas and flies; the word 'ship' is tempting, but it travels through the air.
Types of seagoing ship.Spaceship: A spaceship travels beyond the atmosphere, so is no seagoing vessel, though ships and spacecraft share nautical terms.
Types of seagoing ship.Starship: SpaceX's Starship is the largest rocket ever built, and in fiction starships sail between stars, not seas.
Types of seagoing ship.Zeppelin: Zeppelins were rigid airships named after Count von Zeppelin; the 1937 Hindenburg disaster ended the era.

Jewish holidays.Passover: Passover marks the Exodus from Egypt. Matzah, unleavened bread, is eaten because the Israelites left too fast for dough to rise.
Jewish holidays.Yom Kippur: The Day of Atonement is the holiest day of the Jewish year, observed with a roughly 25-hour fast and prayer.
Jewish holidays.Rosh Hashanah: The Jewish New Year falls in autumn, not January. It is marked by blowing the shofar, a ram's horn, and eating apples with honey.
Jewish holidays.Hanukkah: Hanukkah is an eight-day festival of lights recalling the rededication of the Second Temple. It is minor religiously, though famous because of December.
Jewish holidays.Purim: Purim celebrates the Jews' rescue in ancient Persia, as told in the Book of Esther. Costumes and noisemakers drown out the villain Haman's name.
Jewish holidays.Sukkot: During Sukkot people eat in temporary huts, sukkahs, recalling the Israelites' wandering in the desert.
Jewish holidays.Shavuot: Shavuot marks the giving of the Torah at Mount Sinai. Many Jews eat dairy foods like cheesecake and stay up studying all night.
Jewish holidays.Simchat Torah: Simchat Torah, 'Rejoicing of the Torah', celebrates finishing the yearly Torah reading cycle and starting again with dancing.
Jewish holidays.Tisha B'Av: This fast day mourns the destruction of both Temples in Jerusalem, traditionally on the ninth of Av, and is among the saddest days.
Jewish holidays.Diwali: Diwali is the Hindu, Sikh and Jain festival of lights in autumn. It sounds like Hanukkah's lights, but it is a different tradition.
Jewish holidays.Ramadan: Ramadan is the Muslim month of daily fasting from dawn to dusk. Yom Kippur has a fast too, but it is a single day.
Jewish holidays.Eid al-Fitr: Eid al-Fitr is the Muslim celebration that ends Ramadan, with feasting and charity. It's Islamic, not Jewish.
Jewish holidays.Lent: Lent is the forty-day Christian season of fasting and penitence before Easter, with no place in the Jewish calendar.
Jewish holidays.Easter: Easter celebrates the resurrection of Jesus in the Christian tradition. Its timing has some links to Passover, but it's a separate holiday.
Jewish holidays.Holi: Holi is the Hindu festival of colors, where people throw bright powder in spring. It doesn't belong to the Jewish calendar.
Jewish holidays.Vesak: Vesak marks the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and death, celebrated by Buddhists with lanterns and acts of charity.
Jewish holidays.Epiphany: Epiphany on January 6 is a Christian feast for the Magi's visit to the infant Jesus, so it isn't a Jewish holiday.
Jewish holidays.Advent: Advent is the Christian season of waiting that leads up to Christmas, counted with candles and calendars.
Jewish holidays.Navratri: Navratri is a Hindu festival of nine nights honoring the goddess Durga, so it's not a Jewish holiday.
Jewish holidays.Kwanzaa: Kwanzaa is a week-long African American celebration created in 1966 by Maulana Karenga, not an ancient Jewish holiday.
Jewish holidays.Ash Wednesday: Ash Wednesday starts Lent, when Christians receive ashes on the forehead, so it's Christian, not Jewish.
Jewish holidays.Mardi Gras: Mardi Gras, French for 'Fat Tuesday', is a feast right before Lent, with parades famous in New Orleans.
Jewish holidays.Hogmanay: Hogmanay is the Scottish way of celebrating New Year's Eve, with first-footing and fireworks. It is not Jewish.
Jewish holidays.Obon: Obon is a Japanese Buddhist festival honoring ancestors with lanterns and dances, so it doesn't fit the Jewish calendar.

Fictional ducks.Zazu: Zazu is a hornbill, Mufasa's advisor in The Lion King.
Fictional ducks.Iago: Iago is Jafar's parrot, who squawks insults in Aladdin.
Fictional ducks.Pingu: Pingu is a penguin in a Swiss clay-animated series, who speaks gibberish.
Fictional ducks.Gladstone Gander: Gladstone Gander is Donald's lucky cousin, and he is a goose, as 'gander' means a male goose.
Fictional ducks.Scuttle: Scuttle is a seagull in The Little Mermaid, who misidentifies human objects.
